item.title: Minnesota's largest coal plant is now wiring 1.7 million solar panels powering 150,000 homes
item.description: The largest coal plant in Minnesota is transitioning to embrace renewable energy by hosting a substantial solar farm. Leveraging the existing transmission systems of the coal facility, the Sherco Solar project is now recognized as the most extensive solar installation in the state. This forward-thinking initiative accelerates grid connection for new energy innovations, with exciting plans for future development and battery storage integration.

item.title: A Michigan woman owns 19 acres between two planned Toll Brothers communities
item.description: A woman from Michigan has initiated legal action against Toll Brothers concerning their wastewater management and access rights. Her property, undeveloped, is situated between two upcoming luxury housing estates. The lawsuit alleges that the developers have disregarded her property rights and neglected environmental regulations. She aims to reinstate her access easement and challenge the site plan approvals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Singapore student left home saying she was going to college; hours later her family found her...
item.description: A Singaporean student, Siti Aishah Siregar, disappeared after telling her family she was going to college. Her family discovered her passport missing and a flight ticket to Cambodia in her email. Singapore police confirmed the 20-year-old had already departed the country on an outbound flight. Her father issued an emotional appeal on Facebook for assistance to locate his daughter.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: South Africa released 11 formerly captive elephants onto wild reserves; five years later...
item.description: In an inspiring study, South African elephants reintroduced into reserves demonstrated remarkable behavior akin to that of free-roaming herds. Researchers observed that these elephants not only adapted seamlessly to their natural habitats but also maintained optimal stress hormone levels. This research underscores the potential for long-term captive elephants to regain their independence, offering a promising outlook for the conservation efforts throughout southern Africa.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Arika Kundu, 13, turns peanut shell waste into pesticide remover, competes for $25,000 prize
item.description: Thirteen-year-old Minnesota student Arika Kundu has designed a method that uses discarded peanut shells to help remove pesticide residues from fresh fruits and vegetables. Her project, called LIGNEX, has made her one of 10 finalists in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge. She will now compete for the $25,000 grand prize with guidance from a 3M scientist.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Florida sixth grader Naboshree Santra developed biodegradable soilshade balls designed to...
item.description: An 11-year-old Florida student has reached the finals of a national science competition. Her innovative soilshade balls help farmers conserve water during dry weather conditions. This eco-friendly invention slows evaporation and keeps soil moist for extended periods. She will compete for a $25,000 prize and mentorship from 3M scientists. The competition celebrates young innovators using STEM to solve real-world problems.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tiny reef fish thrived near seabird islands; where rats wiped birds out, marine food chains changed
item.description: Tropical islands are facing a surprising ecological shift as invasive rats disrupt the balance of coral reef ecosystems. By decimating seabird numbers, these rats cut down on essential nutrient contributions to the reefs. As a result, tiny cryptobenthic fish flourish in nutrient-rich spots, while invertebrates find success in less fertile regions, reshaping the food web and highlighting the vulnerable nature of these priceless underwater habitats.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: A wild Himalayan spice is helping 200 families protect 100 sq km of forest while generating an income of Rs 39 lakh
item.description: Indigenous communities in Arunachal Pradesh are now earning livelihoods from a native spice. This wild Himalayan spice, known locally as Khagi, is helping over two hundred families. The community-led system for harvesting and marketing the spice supports forest patrols and biodiversity monitoring. This initiative provides a direct economic incentive for people to protect their forests and agricultural land. The project also contributes to the conservation of important transboundary wildlife habitats.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: 17-year-old proposes hybrid nuclear system to cut Antarctic CO₂ emissions by 3,254 tons
item.description: A young Chilean student has proposed an innovative energy system for Antarctica. This concept combines renewable sources with a nuclear microreactor for reliable power. The system aims to significantly reduce diesel fuel dependence and carbon emissions. It offers a potential solution for powering remote research stations in extreme conditions. This student-led idea highlights future possibilities for sustainable Antarctic energy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New Zealand is investing $202 million in a mega-operation aimed at restoring three islands destroyed by invasive species
item.description: In an inspiring ecological restoration project, New Zealand is teaming up with Māori natives to tackle invasive mammal populations on three major islands, including Maukahuka, Rakiura, and the Chatham archipelago. This extensive collaboration among governmental bodies, local communities, and Indigenous organizations aims to breathe new life into native wildlife. The success of this project could highlight New Zealand's pioneering methods in environmental restoration on the world stage.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Scientists transplanted 42 sea sponges into a polluted Spanish marina; 91.7% of one species survived
item.description: In a remarkable experiment, scientists have introduced sea sponges into a polluted marina in Spain to investigate their resilience. The chicken kidney sponge, a particularly robust species, not only survived for an impressive 455 days but also showcased its remarkable ability to reproduce mobile clones. These developments indicate that sponges may play a critical role in ecological restoration, potentially aiding in the detoxification of contaminated coastal areas.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Africa is pouring in $50 billion to redirect water from Congo River Basin to Lake Chad which has shrunk by 90% since 1960
item.description: Lake Chad's dramatic shrinkage has brought about severe impacts on the lives of millions. To counteract this crisis, governments are investing in initiatives aimed at rehabilitating the lake's ecosystem. A noteworthy solution includes the ambitious Transaqua project, which seeks to channel water from the Congo River back into Lake Chad. This vital endeavor aims not only to replenish the lake but also to foster economic growth in the surrounding regions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 1924, Arctic charr from Lake Geneva were stocked into Lake Allos; a century later...
item.description: Introduced to Lake Allos in 1924, Arctic charr exhibit remarkable metabolic adaptations within just a century. These fish showcase rapid physiological changes, attributed mainly to their phenotypic plasticity, resulting in distinct body shapes. Notably, juveniles from Lake Allos consistently demonstrate elevated metabolic rates, even under controlled conditions. This research underscores the species' ability to swiftly adapt to their ever-changing environmental landscape.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by Leo Tolstoy: 'Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one...'
item.description: According to Leo Tolstoy, true societal change begins with personal evolution. He asserted that individuals must first address their own imperfections. This mindset has significantly shaped leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr. However, in our contemporary society, there is a trend toward prioritizing external grievances over internal growth. To achieve meaningful advancements, it is essential to blend personal honesty with systemic change.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Quazeem Tiamiyu, a student who turned discarded wood into insulation for beverage coolers
item.description: Quazeem Tiamiyu developed safe insulation from wood fiber for beverage coolers. This bio-based component offers an environmentally friendly alternative to toxic polyurethane foam. His innovation utilizes cellulose nanofibrils and wood flour as binders and stabilizers. The new foam demonstrates comparable thermal conductivity to conventional insulation materials. Researchers are working to enhance durability and explore new manufacturing possibilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Spain says most migrants have returned to Morocco after deadly border rush
item.description: Spanish authorities said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border. Officials warned that the death toll could be higher as there may have been additional casualties on the Moroccan side. According to the government, some migrants drowned while others were crushed as they attempted to climb the breakwater supporting the border fence.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Kick streamer Clavicular says Kick spent nearly $700K promoting his clips and gives creators an unlimited clipping budget
item.description: Kick streamer Clavicular revealed the platform funded his viral clip promotions. He stated Kick spent nearly $700,000 in one month for this purpose. This strategy aimed to attract new users to the Kick streaming service. Clavicular believes his content and lifestyle appeal contributed to his rapid growth. Kick's investment highlights a new trend in platform-driven creator promotion.
